q1_issues.issue: The attributive modifier 'algorithmically equivalent' is turned into a coined pairwise relation over the group's members, but the instruction set licenses a literal-head symmetric relation only where a copula predicates it ('the senators are all colleagues'); a descriptive modifier on a definite plural should distribute as a property instead.
The compound symbol algorithmically_equivalent is given a genus atom but is never predicated of anything, so the decomposition dangles — the modifier was encoded as the relation instead.
'random' is predicated of the group symbol sk_way_1, the group-as-object reading the plural rules explicitly forbid; a descriptive modifier on a plural must distribute over the members.
The definite plural subject with a distributive predicate ('can be defined') gets the group event only, with no per-member distribution rule alongside it.

q2_gaps: attributive relational/symmetric adjective inside an NP ('these mutually equivalent Ns') — the symmetric-relation machinery is defined only for predicative use, and the plural-modifier rule offers only a distributing property or a fusing classifier, neither of which records the mutuality the phrase states
notes: The agentless passive with (Can e), Theme for the defined sequences, the demonstrative-plural group witness, and the counted 'three ways' group with Cardinality all follow the instruction set, and (In ...) is acceptable as the surface-preposition oblique. AlgorithmicallyEquivalent has the shape of the licensed group-symmetric head but nothing here predicates it copularly, which is the condition the open-class licence names.
